# eyg_interpreter · v6.0.0

Source: https://eyg-interpreter.hexdocs.pm/

# eyg_interpreter

Gleam implementation of the [EYG](https://eyg.run) language.
This implementation runs on JavaScript runtimes and works in the browser.

```
gleam add eyg_interpreter@1
```
This library defines two execution modes:

- expression - always returns a value
- block - optionally returns a value and the final environment.

If in doubt use the expression module. Block is useful for creating shells (or REPLs, terminals, consoles).

```
import eyg/interpreter/expression
import eyg/ir/tree as ir
pub fn main() {
  let source = ir.let_("x", ir.integer(5), ir.variable("x"))
  let scope = []
  expression.execute(source, scope)
  // => value.Integer(5)
}
```
Further documentation can be found at [https://hexdocs.pm/eyg_interpreter](https://hexdocs.pm/eyg_interpreter).

## Development

```
gleam run   # Run the project
gleam test  # Run the tests
```

---

# eyg_interpreter · v6.0.0

Source: https://eyg-interpreter.hexdocs.pm/index.html

# eyg_interpreter

Gleam implementation of the [EYG](https://eyg.run) language.
This implementation runs on JavaScript runtimes and works in the browser.

```
gleam add eyg_interpreter@1
```
This library defines two execution modes:

- expression - always returns a value
- block - optionally returns a value and the final environment.

If in doubt use the expression module. Block is useful for creating shells (or REPLs, terminals, consoles).

```
import eyg/interpreter/expression
import eyg/ir/tree as ir
pub fn main() {
  let source = ir.let_("x", ir.integer(5), ir.variable("x"))
  let scope = []
  expression.execute(source, scope)
  // => value.Integer(5)
}
```
Further documentation can be found at [https://hexdocs.pm/eyg_interpreter](https://hexdocs.pm/eyg_interpreter).

## Development

gleam test  # Run the tests

pub type Reason(m, c) {
  NotAFunction(
```
[value.Value](value.html#Value)(m, c))
  UndefinedVariable(String)
  UndefinedBuiltin(String)
  UndefinedReference([v1.Cid](https://hexdocs.pm/multiformats/4.0.0/multiformats/cid/v1.html#Cid))
  UndefinedRelease(package: String, release: Int, module: [v1.Cid](https://hexdocs.pm/multiformats/4.0.0/multiformats/cid/v1.html#Cid))
  UndefinedRelative(location: String)
  Vacant
  NoMatch(term: [value.Value](value.html#Value)(m, c))
  UnhandledEffect(String, [value.Value](value.html#Value)(m, c))
  IncorrectTerm(expected: String, got: [value.Value](value.html#Value)(m, c))
  MissingField(String)
  Unrepresentable(builtin: String, args: List([value.Value](value.html#Value)(m, c)))
}

    [state.Stack](https://eyg-interpreter.hexdocs.pm/state.html#Stack)(m),
  ),
)Resume the interpretation loop with a value from a previous break position. This can be used to resume after any break but is normally used to implement effects and reference lookup

---

# eyg/interpreter/simple_debug · eyg_interpreter · v6.0.0

Source: https://eyg-interpreter.hexdocs.pm/eyg/interpreter/simple_debug.html

Pretty-printed representation of EYG values.

Output is laid out by `glam` so that small structures collapse onto a
single line and only larger structures break across multiple lines. The
returned string is intended for human consumption — applications that
need machine-readable output should serialise the value themselves.

    `pub const default_width: Int`

    Default width used when none is supplied.

    `pub fn describe(reason: `[break.Reason](break.html#Reason)(a, b)) -> String

    Describe a reason to stop execution.

    `pub fn hint(reason: `[break.Reason](break.html#Reason)(a, b)) -> String

    Suggest a possible fix for an execution error.

    `pub fn inspect(value: `[value.Value](value.html#Value)(a, b)) -> String

    Inspect a value at the default width.

    `pub fn render(value: `[value.Value](value.html#Value)(a, b), width: Int) -> String

    Render a value with an explicit line-width budget. A larger width keeps
more on one line; a smaller width causes earlier breaking.

---
